facts.text: The package is a PyBullet implementation of the OpenAI Gym multi-goal robotics environment and uses a Kuka iiwa14 7DoF arm with a robotiq85 or a parallel jaw gripper
Observation is a dictionary containing the state, desired goal, achieved goal and other sensory data
The documented way to create an environment is the make_env(...) method
make_env maps task 'block_stack' to the entry point pybullet_multigoal_gym.envs.task_envs.kuka_multi_step_envs:KukaBlockStackEnv
make_env builds the environment id from the task tag, gripper, render, reward, joint-control and image flags and appends -v0
make_env registers the multi-block tasks with the task constructor kwargs and the caller's max_episode_steps
make_env returns gym.make(env_id)
make_env defaults max_episode_steps to 50
KukaBlockStackEnv defaults distance_threshold to 0.05 and num_block to 5
KukaBlockStackEnv passes grasping=True, joint_control=False, end_effector_start_on_table=False, obj_range=0.15 and target_range=0.15 to its multi-block base class
BaseBulletMGEnv is a gym.Env
The base environment's constructor defaults are seed 0, gravity 9.81, timestep 0.002 s and frame_skip 20, and it seeds itself with seed 0
dt is timestep * frame_skip; the comment gives 0.002 * 20 = 0.04 seconds at the defaults
seed delegates to gym.utils.seeding.np_random and returns [seed]
reset(test=False) resets the robot and the task and returns the observation
step applies the action, computes the reward from the achieved and desired goals, and returns (obs, reward, False, info) with info['goal_achieved']

The environment owns an in-process PyBullet BulletClient (DIRECT by default, GUI when render=True) and sets gravity, fixedTimeStep = timestep * frame_skip, solver iterations and substeps; real-time simulation is off
The action space is the robot's action space
For non-image observations the observation space is a Dict of four Box(-inf, inf) float32 members named state, policy_state, achieved_goal and desired_goal
With grasping True, joint_control False and no primitive or end-effector rotation control, Kuka.action_space is Box(-1, 1) with 4 elements

Each block contributes world position, relative position to the gripper, world euler orientation, and relative linear and angular velocities to the state, and its relative position to the policy state
state is the gripper xyz, finger closeness, gripper velocity and finger velocity followed by the block states; policy_state is the gripper xyz, finger closeness and the relative block positions
state and policy_state are clipped to [-5, 5]
The observation dict has keys observation, policy_state, achieved_goal and desired_goal
The sparse reward is -not_achieved and the dense reward is -distance, where distance is the Euclidean norm of the achieved minus desired goal and not_achieved is distance > distance_threshold
The runtime dependencies are setuptools, pybullet~=3.0.6, gym~=0.17.3, numpy~=1.19.4, numba and numpy-quaternion

determinism.notes: reset(seed) reaches the legacy env.seed() path and cap.world.seed.v1 sets the seed of the next reset; the fake draws its placeholder block positions with Python's random.Random while upstream seeds gym.utils.seeding.np_random, so one seed repeats on the fake but gives different numbers than upstream, and no trajectory of the two was compared

gaps: no dynamics: the fake moves the end effector by a fixed placeholder displacement and has no PyBullet, rigid-body, inverse-kinematics, contact, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model; the upstream environment would be an F1 PyBullet model, not this

only the default non-image BlockStack configuration is modelled (parallel jaw or robotiq85, no joint control, no task decomposition, no curriculum, no grip-informed goal); image observations, goal images, depth and point clouds are refused by the fake

observations are placeholder Python float lists; upstream returns float32 numpy arrays, and the reported lengths are the upstream composition for five blocks (83 state, 19 policy, 15 achieved and 15 desired values), not measured runs
the fake applies the 50-step time limit that make_env registers through max_episode_steps; the upstream task's own step() always returns done False and the limit comes from gym's TimeLimit wrapper
the fake draws the initial state with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy's generator, so one seed gives different numbers on the two
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state pair
the upstream id is registered only when make_env is called, so the sim path (gym.make of the id) was not run; the fake is the only declared backend
no physical device is modelled and the simulator was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
